title: Chennedy Carter’s turbulent WNBA career continues after she was waived by Las Vegas Aces
content:
The Las Vegas Aces waived guard Chennedy Carter on Tuesday, in one of the biggest moves at the WNBA’s midseason cut-down deadline.

Carter made the Aces ‘ regular season roster on a non-guaranteed, veteran-minimum contract valued at $277,500 after signing a training camp deal in April. Teams had until 5 p.m. (ET) on Tuesday to waive players on non-guaranteed contracts before their contracts became fully guaranteed.

The Aces’ decision to waive Carter means they will not have to pay out the rest of her deal.

This is the fourth WNBA team Carter has departed under unfavorable terms.

There had been high hopes for Carter, a dynamic guard, when she joined the Aces and started the season on a tear, averaging 19 points, 2.5 rebounds and 1.8 assists off the bench. But her role changed drastically after she took to social media to air grievances following the Aces’ 95-87 loss to the Dallas Wings on May 28. She appeared to take issue with her role in Las Vegas, saying in part, “Y’all can hollar (sic) at me when my leash is off, too.”  That remark was part of a lengthier response to fans commenting on her inability to slow down Wings rookie Azzi Fudd, who scored 22 in that game.

Carter played fewer than 10 minutes in the Aces’ following game, against the Golden State Valkyries.

She missed three games at the start of June with a left leg injury and returned for just two games before being ruled out again with an illness. She returned to the Aces’ rotation on June 28 against the Sky and finished with 11 points against her former team.

In her final game for the Aces on July 5 against the Indiana Fever, she was held scoreless in 15 minutes off the bench.

Carter is one of the quickest guards in the WNBA and almost impossible to stop when she’s getting downhill and attacking the rim. But her behavior off the court has led to her early dismissal from multiple WNBA teams.

She was selected by the Atlanta Dream in 2020 with the fourth pick. The following season, she was suspended for “conduct detrimental to the team.” In 2022, she was traded to the Los Angeles Sparks and played just one season for the organization before being waived the following March.

After not playing in the WNBA in 2023, she was signed by the Sky in 2024, where she averaged a team-high 17.5 points per game, 3.5 rebounds and 3.1 assists. The Sky ultimately decided not to extend a qualifying offer to Carter that offseason, making her an unrestricted free agent. She went unsigned in 2025 and ended up playing in Mexico and China.

In a related move, the Aces signed 6-foot-4 guard/forward Justine Pissott, who was signed to a developmental player contract with Indiana. She played one preseason game for the Fever, their win against the New York Liberty on April 25, and finished with eight points, shooting 2-of-3 from 3-point range.
